text:
maria.product: Heads-up — we need to finalize the v2 API surface + deprecation timeline for v1. Customer asks are stacking up (tool-calling changes, structured outputs). Can we carve scope and landing criteria today?
ashwin.eng: +1. key tradeoffs: strict breaking changes vs keeping shims. Shims add maintenance cost but reduce customer churn.
lee.platform: For Dedicated/Private we can expose a compatibility toggle at the router level (header or route flag). Would prefer header-based first: `X-Redwood-Compat: v1|v2` to avoid route explosion.
eva.csm: Customers expect 6–12 months notice for major changes. A few HS customers already asked to keep v1 behavior for tool calling because they rely on old function payload shapes.
connor.se: We should list every surface that changes: chat/completions param names, streaming semantics, embeddings vector shape metadata, rerank API signature, tool/function calling (args reshape), structured output schema envelopes. I can draft a mapping.
maria.product: Good. Proposed high-level plan: 1) publish a migration guide + SDK shims, 2) opt-in v2 for 3 months, 3) soft-deprecation notices, 4) force migration after 9 months. Thoughts?
nashwin.eng: I worry about the "force" after 9 months unless we have telemetry showing migration progress. Suggest criteria gates: - 80% of active users migrated OR - error rate spike risk below threshold. Also require 95th latency within +10% of v1.
lee.platform: Telemetry available: per-route adoption, error rate, tail latency. We can build a "compat dashboard" in Console. Rollout toggles: per-customer flag, region, and canary groups (1/10/50/100%).
eva.csm: Add customer communication steps: pre-announce (60d), migration docs + migration office hours (30d), follow-up reminders (14d, 7d), and targeted SE assistance for flagged customers.
connor.se: On the technical side, propose two compatibility layers: 1) request-surface shim (translate v1 payload to v2 internally), 2) response-format shim (wrap v2 responses to look like v1). Make shims opt-in and eventually removeable.
maria.product: That helps define scope. Now specifics: function calling changes — v2 returns `tool_call` object instead of inline args, and supports structured arg schemas. Do we keep auto-arg coercion for v1?
nashwin.eng: Keep coercion for v1 routes for the deprecation window. For v2 require strict validation against declared schema. That lets us tighten guarantees going forward. We'll add warnings in logs when coercion occurs.
lee.platform: Implementation note: for hosted API, shims run in the router; for dedicated/private, we can provide a shim sidecar package customers can opt into. We'll document config: `compat.mode: "shim" | "passthrough" | "strict"`.
eva.csm: Customers on Dedicated will need a clear upgrade path — shipping a sidecar is fine but must be supported for 12 months. Also include an FAQ on performance impact of shims.
connor.se: Migration guide table of contents I'll draft: 1) Breaking changes matrix (v1 -> v2) 2) Quick fixes per SDK 3) Tool-calling examples 4) Structured output mapping 5) Test harness and sample prompts 6) Rollback instructions 7) Known gaps.
maria.product: Launch criteria checklist (proposed): - Migration guide published + docs PR merged - SDKs (python/js) have transport-level toggles + example migrations - Console shows compat dashboard - Canary rollout to internal + 3 customers with no regressions - Performance guardrails: p50/p95 within +10% vs baseline - E2E tests cover function calling + structured output - CS playbook ready. Approve?
ashwin.eng: Add: automated compare tests that run v1 vs v2 responses on canonical prompt sets and flag semantic regressions. We'll gate on no >2% regression on core prompts.
lee.platform: We'll add a runtime flag `X-Redwood-Compat-Mode` for internal canaries and `X-Redwood-Compat` for customer selection. We'll also ship `--compat-shim` for sidecar.
eva.csm: For timelines, customers expect: pre-announce in 60 days, opt-in window 90 days, targeted assistance until 180 days, then start deprecation wind-down. So overall ~6 months visibility + 6 months support.
maria.product: OK propose official schedule: Week 0: announce; Week 4: migration guide + SDK toggles; Week 6–10: canaries + customer pilots; Week 12: opt-in v2 open; Week 24: start strong deprecation notices; Week 36: remove shims for hosted default but keep per-customer flag for another 6 months. Is that too long?
nashwin.eng: That gives engineers runway but delays value of v2. Could shorten to 24–30 weeks total. Let's mark schedule flexible based on adoption metrics.
connor.se: One more: automated tool-calling compatibility harness. We should produce a repo with sample functions and prebuilt validators so customers can run their tests locally. I'll own it.
lee.platform: Ops considerations: deprecation of v1 route names will need nginx/router redirects and a migration job to update internal configs. We'll prepare a migration playbook for infra.
maria.product: Action items: - @connor.se draft the breaking changes matrix and sample harness (due in 5 business days) - @ashwin.eng define the shim behavior and performance budget (5 days) - @lee.platform spec header flags and toggle apis + console UX (7 days) - @eva.csm prepare customer comms draft and SE availability plan (3 days) - I'll consolidate schedule and PRD after those artifacts.
eva.csm: FYI: two customers (AcmeHealth, FinTrust) flagged they will need dedicated support for function arg shape changes. I'll open tickets.
nashwin.eng: Also propose adding deprecation headers in responses during opt-in window: `Warning: Redwood-API v1 deprecated; migrate to v2` with link to guide.
deploy-bot: Scheduled: canary-deploy v2-shim (internal) starting at 1768004400 by @deploy-bot.
maria.product: Great. If nobody objects, I'll lock this plan and create the PRD doc. Please add comments in the PRD draft when I share. :thumbsup:
nashwin.eng: :thumbsup:
lee.platform: LGTM
connor.se: On it
eva.csm: Thanks — will coordinate with AcmeHealth and FinTrust."
